title: Three Weeks and One Short Envelope
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：message　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 message 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the postman ① sent the message that no sender in the office would have counted, and he said the sending was the whole of the week. The ② message, meaning the note itself and not the envelope, ran three weeks and stayed uncounted in the book; a message, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ message in that office had the same short envelope beside it, and the ④ message at the far box, meaning the parcel they kept for the children to fetch and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A message, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the postman said the counting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the message was the whole of the matter, meaning the meaning and not the note. The ⑥ message, meaning the meaning and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; message, he said, is either something you send or the only word that means both a note and a meaning. He said the meaning is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ message had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short envelope. The ⑧ message of the whole thing, the postman wrote in June, was one office and three weeks of counting; message, he said, is either the parcel at the far box or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ message I remember is the note counted in the list, which closed in 1974 and is still counted as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ message, my mother said in 1976, is the only note that improves by being counted; every message, she said, is a meaning that has agreed to look like a note. She said the meaning was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 消息；口信（指邮局里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 消息；口信（指那条消息本身，与薄薄的信封相对）
C. 固定搭配：send the message 捎这一条消息
D. n. 消息；口信（指留给孩子们取的那一件）
E. n. 消息之事（抽象总称，指一处邮局的消息之事）
F. n. 消息；口信（指收发清单里写到、被清点的那一条）
G. n. 消息、心意（指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 心意（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: sent the message that no sender in the office would have counted
The message, meaning the note itself and not the envelope
the message at the far box
the message was the whole of the matter
the message had become a line in a list
The message of the whole thing
A message, my mother said in 1976

answers.why: send the message 意为“捎这一条消息”，1967 年那位邮差把邮局里没有一位寄信人肯清点的一条消息做了一遍。
message 意为“消息；口信”，指那条消息本身而不是薄薄的信封，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被清点。
message 意为“消息；口信”，指邮局里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一个薄薄的信封。
message 意为“消息；口信”，指最远那只信箱的留给孩子们取的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
message 意为“消息、心意”，指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这条心意就是那件事的全部。
message 意为“心意”，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西而不是那条消息，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
message 意为“消息；口信”，指收发清单里写到、被清点的那一条，到 1972 年这一条成了收发清单里的一行。
message 意为“消息之事”，邮差六月写道，整件事的消息之事是一处邮局和三个星期的清点。
message 意为“消息；口信”，我记得的是收发清单里清点过的那一条，1974 年送完了，至今仍被说成邮局里最安静的一条。
message 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，消息是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的消息。
